decision_scope: Fresh current-dev representation-isolated CPU/live-structure-heap evidence. Final PR readiness awaits separately measured current-dev application profile; this microbenchmark does not establish UI performance.

method.sdk: Dart3.13.5 AOT for timings; separate JIT VM for heap
method.samples: 4 separate VM processes x8 timed samples per side/case=32; correctness preflight then4 explicit warmups per side/process/case
method.median: Arithmetic mean of the two central observations for even sample sizes (statistics.median)
method.p95: Nearest rank ceil(.95*n),31st sorted observation for n32
method.candidate_normalization: Candidate scanOnly uses current-dev eager list construction, isolating representation from its separate lazy-expand optimization
method.source_guards: Current-dev no-op check retained; existing revision-before-listEquals optimization is already in both refs and is not credited to the PR

interpretation: Large genuine savings remain in initial sparse representation, changed ranges on prepared sparse/full chunked state, and eviction from prepared full chunked state.
Changed updates starting from flat full content, eviction starting from flat full content, and sparse count worker CPU are slower in all4 process medians.
Full count worker pooled median is about4.1% slower, but oneprocess favors the candidate; do not claim a consistent regression.
rawCharactersExceed is measured only below10000 lines with the exact1MiB cutoff, since production skips it for larger ranges. Absolute added preflight time is well below1ms in this fixture.

The combined partial/warm/full/edit/hide sequence measures a synthetic composition of real list operations; it is not observed app lifecycle latency. Normal range-based warming emits batches, not FullBookContent. Full-content flat handoff occurs in preview fallback and its costs are conditional.
countChunks CPU runs in a worker for large ranges in production; measured CPU differences are not UI frame timings. Isolate transfer, scheduling, I/O and Flutter rendering are excluded.
Shared preallocated plain ASCII strings isolate representation and current plain-text counting. HTML, notes, markup and diverse real book texts are out of scope.
Heap values are post-GC JIT live-object deltas for list structure with shared text excluded, including protocol noise. They are not total app memory, RSS, allocation throughput or AOT heap.
Microbenchmarks cannot resolve the earlier mixed frame/jump results, nor remove the need to validate the current-dev integrated candidate.
